items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Didn't ask 'How are you today?', gave no upfront agenda statement (what's covered + rough time), and never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.

2_probe: Never captured zip codes for either address, didn't ask about narrow hallways/tight turns, packing needs, storage stops, additional stops, or the 'what are you most worried about' stressor question.
3_pricing: No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000) not mentioned, Meet Your Mover email not mentioned, On-Time Guarantee not mentioned.
4_clock: Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens.
5_estimate: Didn't specify number of trucks, didn't tie stairs/elevator or walking distance into the time estimate, no equivalents used to make the hours tangible.
6_save_your_ass: Entire prep speech skipped -- no mention of pre-move consolidation, the carload tip, or how prep shortens the bill.
7_quote_booking: No mention that no deposit is required, no 'reply with any corrections' ask, didn't ask if she had any other questions before ending, didn't give hours or how to reach the office.
9_bonus: No rapport-building or humor with the customer, and no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60 cents/lb baseline) given.
top_strength: Danah gathered a complete two-address move profile (size, floors, elevator, boxes, walk distances) in under 6 minutes, and stepped in immediately when the assigned rep went to lunch -- "let me go ahead and help you out" -- so the customer wasn't made to wait or call back.
coaching_note: Danah, your intake pace is good, but you're skipping the two things that actually move a prospect to book: the differentiators (No Worries damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the full Save Your Ass prep speech, which is the section that most affects final bill size. You also never locked down her name correctly ("Michaela"/"Mickayla"/"Mickaela" -- it's Makayla). Close every call with "no deposit required" and "any other questions before I let you go" -- this one just trailed off after she asked for pricing in writing, which is likely why it didn't convert to a booking on the spot.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative throughout but transactional -- no affirmations, humor, or acknowledgment beyond the task, though she did proactively cover for a teammate at lunch.
